memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: God heard the boy crying, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What is the matter, Hagar? Do not be afraid; God has heard the boy crying as he lies there. Lift the boy up and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation." Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. - Gen 21:17-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"God heard the boy crying." What tender words. In her despair, Hagar thought all was lost - but God had heard. And notice what God does not do: He does not scold Hagar for her despair. He speaks gently: "Do not be afraid; God has heard." Then, remarkably, "God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water." The water was there all along. She simply couldn't see it until God opened her eyes.

There is a profound truth here. Sometimes God's provision is already near, and our despair blinds us to it. Hagar was sitting a stone's throw from a well and did not see it, because grief and fear had closed her eyes. God's answer was not to create a well out of nothing, but to open her eyes to the provision already present.

How often are we the same? In our distress, we cannot see the help that God has already placed nearby - the resources, the people, the mercies right in front of us. We are so consumed by the problem that we miss the provision. Sometimes what we most need is not a new miracle but opened eyes.

This is a prayer worth praying often: "Lord, open my eyes." Like Elisha's servant who couldn't see the armies of God until his eyes were opened (2 Kings 6:17), we need God to help us see what is already there. Whatever desert you're in, ask God to open your eyes. His provision may be nearer than your despair allows you to see.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Might God's provision be nearer than your despair lets you see?
- What would it mean to pray, "Lord, open my eyes"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, in my distress I often cannot see the help You have already placed near me. Open my eyes to Your provision. Thank You that You hear my cry and that Your mercies may be nearer than I know.
Amen.
